Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

random adjective and adverb

also at random, randomly, by chance, haphazard, any old

classical

Ter. Ph. 5.1.30 (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Div. 2.141: cāsū nōnnumquam forte temere concurrerent (Lewis & Short)

1temere: short final e (Lewis & Short tĕmĕrē). A petrified locative of an s-stem noun *temes- “darkness” (Proto-Italic *temesi), whose ending gives a short -e: “in the dark”, so “blindly” (de Vaan 609, s.v. temere).

temere1

adverb

at random, without plan; heedlessly

Blindly, without design: things that happen forte temere, by mere chance, or that are done at random. Its commonest sense is “rashly” (cavētō aliēnam disciplīnam temere contemnās, Cato Agr. 1.4).

Other words

  • 2fortuītus: long i (Lewis & Short marks the vowel common). Long in Hor. C. 2.15.17 and Phaedr. 2.4.4, short only in Petronius, Juvenal and Manilius (Lewis & Short, s.v.); the classical scansion is long.

    fortuītus2, fortuīta, fortuītum — chance, accidental

    also used · classical · Cic. Top. 73: concursiō rērum fortuītārum (Lewis & Short); Cic. de Or. 1.150: subita et fortuīta ōrātiō (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Of what happens by chance, a chance meeting, an unplanned speech; not of a thing picked at random.

  • quīlibet, quaelibet, quodlibet — any at all, a random one

    pronoun (adjective), any … you please · also used · classical · Plaut. Poen. 4.2.38: alium quemlibet (Lewis & Short); Cic. Rosc. Am. 8: quaelibet minima rēs (Lewis & Short)

    For “pick a random one”: “any one you like, the first that comes”.

Examples

  • quam saepe forte temere ēveniunt, quae nōn audeās optāre!

    how often things happen by mere chance that you wouldn’t dare to wish for!Ter. Ph. 5.1.30 (Lewis & Short)

  • Chartam quamlibet sūme.

    Take any card.composed

See also happen, chance.
